guyan.logline_en: You duck into a second-hand bookshop before closing to escape the rain — and find a line written on the flyleaf that reads like it was meant for you.
hold_en: He nods, slowly, the way he does when he is memorising something.
"Take your time," he says. "The rain isn't in a hurry either."
Dango settles between you, and he takes that as permission to stay quiet a while.
"I'd like to hear the rest of that," he says, and goes pink at his own boldness.

chapters.goal_en: Make him want to keep the lights on a little longer for you
chapters.scene_en: a bookshop at dusk, warm lamplight, soft rain outside

options.text_en: "Did you write it?"
(Read the line aloud, softly.)
"I'll buy this one."
"I'll return it another day, then."
"It's fine — a walk in the rain isn't so bad."
"Then what about you?"

chapters.goal_en: Find out why he keeps this shop all alone
chapters.scene_en: the bookshop days later, afternoon light slanting in, dust drifting in the beam

options.text_en: "I think it's the only place lately I've wanted to stay."
"How is keeping what you love ever a waste?"
"What do you think?"
"I'll keep it."
"Did you write it for me?"
"Keep it — I'll come read it next time."

chapters.goal_en: Read what he won't say out loud
chapters.scene_en: a street corner late at night, rain pouring, the bookshop's lamp the only light on

options.text_en: "Then don't. Let me say it first."
"I'll wait for you to finish. I'm not in a hurry."
"First hold the umbrella straight — stop getting soaked."
"Come up for hot tea first — you're drenched."
"Tomorrow… I'll come find you at the shop."
(Rise on your toes and hold the umbrella over his head.)

chapters.goal_en: Decide whether to help him fight for this shop
chapters.scene_en: inside the shop, an opened letter on the table, Dango circling him uneasily

options.text_en: "Don't sign it. I'll help you find another way."
"It's your shop. If you want to keep it, keep it. I'm on your side."
"Sign it or not, you won't lose this place — it's already inside you."
Make the tea. I'll stay for the tea.
"Then don't. This one's mine now."
(Cross to him and put the book back on the shelf together.)
"Keep it, and you keep every beginning we've had."

chapters.goal_en: Hear him finish the sentence he never could
chapters.scene_en: the bookshop reopened, a new sign above the door, clear skies outside the window

options.text_en: (Take his hand so he stops trembling.)
"Whatever you say — my answer is yes."
"The truth is, I already understood it."
Finish the sentence first. Everything else can wait.

endings.title_en: The Kind of Love That Takes Its Time
Only a Line Between the Pages

ethan.title_en: The Light on the Top Floor
ethan.logline_en: You got off on the wrong floor — and walked into the private hour of a man who never stops for anyone.
hold_en: He doesn't fill the silence. He lets it sit, and watches what you do with it.
"Keep going," he says. "I'm not going anywhere tonight."
He turns the glass a quarter turn on the table and doesn't drink from it.
"Say that again," he says. "Slower. I want to be sure I heard it."

chapters.goal_en: Make him remember your name
chapters.scene_en: the top floor of an office tower at midnight, one office still lit

options.text_en: "The elevator isn't fixed yet."
"Because you haven't."
(Say nothing. Just look at him.)

chapters.goal_en: Find out why he's here every night
chapters.scene_en: the same rooftop bar, a week later — this time he's expecting you

options.text_en: "Someone who locked himself on the top floor."
"Someone who's very good at control."
"I don't know yet. That's why I'm still here."

chapters.goal_en: See who he is when he's not on the top floor
chapters.scene_en: a rainy night across town, a small noodle shop still open

options.text_en: "Have a safe flight."
"Why are you telling me this?"
"Then I'll come find you Thursday."

chapters.goal_en: Decide whether to stand on his side
chapters.scene_en: a corporate gala, flashbulbs and champagne

options.text_en: "Is the document real?"
"Not here."
"I don't need to ask."
Not tonight — but don't take me home yet.

chapters.goal_en: Get him to say what he actually wants
chapters.scene_en: back on the top floor — the city below, and the lights off

options.text_en: (Wait. Let him finish.)
"You can say it. I'm here."
"Take New York."
Slower than this. I want the whole thing.

endings.title_en: The Light Stays On For You
Just a Light on a Top Floor

luxingye.logline_en: The whole world screams for him — but the only one he wants to see the real him is you, in row seven.
hold_en: He drops his chin onto the back of the chair and grins up at you. "Go on. I'm listening."
"You know nobody talks to me like this," he says. "Don't stop on my account."
He plays two notes, stops, and looks at you instead of the strings.
"Say more things," he says. "I like your voice better than the room."

chapters.goal_en: Make him drop the idol mask for one minute
chapters.scene_en: backstage after a concert, neon signs still glowing, just the two of you

options.text_en: "I want that grain of rice on your face."
"I'm not a fan. So you can relax."
"Just now — you looked better than you do on stage."
"Depends how you do out there."
"Row seven. I have a ticket, you know."
"I should go — don't let me hold you up."

chapters.goal_en: Find out what the 'perfect idol' is really carrying
chapters.scene_en: an empty rehearsal room late at night, one lamp on, guitar in his arms

options.text_en: "I want the you who sneaks rice balls and admits he's tired."
"I don't know the stage one. The one I know is this one, right here."
"Depends if you'll still dare eat rice balls in front of me."
"Mystery person? That's just me."
"If I were scared, I wouldn't be here at midnight."
"Won't this cause trouble for you?"

chapters.goal_en: In front of thousands, catch the words meant only for you
chapters.scene_en: a sold-out arena, a sea of glow-sticks, you in row seven

options.text_en: (Raise your glow-stick and make a heart at him, in the sea of light.)
(Stand and shout back: "I like you too!")
(Do nothing but nod, seriously, across the sea of people.)
"You dared shout it to thousands — I dare stand beside you."
"Why would I? You finally got to sing that song."
"It was reckless. But I like you reckless."

chapters.goal_en: Decide which side to stand on — him, or the industry's rules
chapters.scene_en: the corridor outside a company boardroom, suits filling the glass-walled room

options.text_en: "Don't sign. I don't need you to lie for me, and I won't let you ruin yourself for me. We'll figure it out together."
"It's your life. Whatever you choose, I'm with you."
"If signing saves everything you have, I can step into the background first."
Not tonight. Sit on the floor and eat noodles with me.
(Hold out your hand, palm up, waiting for him to take it.)
"Step out. Whatever storm's out here, I'll face it with you."
"Don't bet everything on me — I'm not worth losing the whole world."

chapters.goal_en: On the smallest stage, catch his truest words
chapters.scene_en: a tiny livehouse — no trending topics, no flashbulbs, a few dozen people in the seats

options.text_en: "I will. But next time — I want to sit on stage, right beside you."
"I will. I stopped being the fan in row seven long ago — I'm yours."
(Pull him up off the floor and kiss him in front of everyone.)
Ask me again when the storm's over.

endings.title_en: From Row Seven to the Stage
The Show With an Audience of One

liam.logline_en: He ran into a burning building to save a stranger — and walked out of the rubble holding a watch that turns out to be yours.
hold_en: He leans back against the tailgate and gives you his whole attention, which is a lot of attention.
"Keep talking," he says. "I've got nowhere I need to be till six."
Biscuit sighs and flops across both your feet, pinning you there.
"That's the good stuff," he says. "Say the rest of it."

chapters.goal_en: Make this golden-retriever of a man remember you as more than 'the new neighbor'
chapters.scene_en: his pickup truck bed at sunset, tailgate down, two root beers, dog at your feet

options.text_en: "I just wanted somewhere the sink gets fixed by a cute neighbor."
"I wanted a place that feels like home. Haven't had one in a while."
"Peace and quiet. Then a firefighter and a dog showed up."
"Depends. You cooking?"
"I'll be there. Save me a seat."
"Go save the world first. Then we'll talk."

chapters.goal_en: See the side this always-smiling man keeps tucked away
chapters.scene_en: a backyard cookout at night, string lights in the trees, the grill crackling, the dog weaving through the crowd

options.text_en: "So — are you okay, Liam?"
"Then lean on me for once. I can take it."
"Every day. Guess that's why I moved next to you."
"Same time next week? I'll bring the bad jokes."
"Easy's good. You've earned easy, Liam."
(Rise on your toes, kiss his cheek quickly, and turn inside.)

chapters.goal_en: On his most dangerous night, be the reason he wants to make it back
chapters.scene_en: late at night, an apartment in the neighborhood ablaze, thick smoke, sirens and firelight lighting up the whole street

options.text_en: "I'm gonna tell them you ran into a fire to save an old man's life. And a watch."
"Being scared and going in anyway — that's the bravest thing there is."
"Your secret's safe. But you're not doing the scared part alone anymore."
"It's the last thing I have from my grandmother. You just ran into a fire with it."
"It matters. But right now, honestly? You matter more."
"She used to say: hold on to the people who show up. You showed up."

chapters.goal_en: In the choice he'd shoulder alone, let him know he doesn't have to
chapters.scene_en: the fire station garage at night, Liam alone on a bench by the engine, a letter in his hand

options.text_en: "Take it. And take me with you. I didn't move here for the town — I moved for you."
"Don't take it for me. But don't turn it down for me either. Let's figure it out — together."
"You've saved everyone else's home for ten years. Go build one you get to keep."
Take the couch, Reyes. I'll still be here in the morning.
"Then stop running. Stand still a second. I'll be right here."
"That something isn't going anywhere. Whatever you choose."
"Good. Because I'm the thing, and I'm not on fire, and I'm not leaving."

chapters.goal_en: Hear this man who always puts others first say what he wants for himself
chapters.scene_en: his backyard at sunset, two chairs on the newly-built porch, two root beers still on the tailgate

options.text_en: (Take the key and slide it onto your keyring.) "Then stop calling it my house and your house. It's home now."
"The job's yours. But I've got one condition: you come home to me alive, every single time."
"I gave you a key first, you know. The one to me. You just took a while to notice."
Ask me once more when you know what you want to do.

endings.title_en: The Neighbor Who Took His Time
The Door Next Door That Never Knocked Again

adrian.title_en: The Song He Won't Admit He Wrote
adrian.logline_en: He writes songs for the whole world — but there's one he never releases and flatly denies writing. It's about you.
hold_en: He doesn't answer. He watches you, which from him is the same as answering.
"Don't stop," he says, short. "I'm not bored yet."
He mutes the strings with his palm so he can hear you better, and pretends he didn't.
"Again," he says. "That part. Say it again."

chapters.goal_en: Make this man who's bored of everyone look at you twice
chapters.scene_en: an empty stage after the show, one spotlight left on, his guitar still humming

options.text_en: "The thing you were just humming? That one I'd listen to."
"I listen. I just don't scream about it."
"I'm here to coil cables, not stroke your ego."
"Maybe I'll be here. Maybe I won't."
"I'll come. But not for the show."
"Four's early for a rockstar."

chapters.goal_en: Find out what the man who's untamed on stage is really writing about
chapters.scene_en: the makeshift recording corner in the back of the tour bus, 3 a.m., one warm lamp, crumpled lyric sheets on the floor

options.text_en: "Because the guy at 3 a.m. writing on the floor is the real one. I like him better."
"Trouble's fine. I just don't do fake. And you're not fake in here."
"Maybe I just wanted to hear the song you keep hiding."
"He's a friend. You can stop torturing that guitar string now."
"You know, jealousy's a good look on a songwriter."
(Say nothing. Cross over and take the pen out of his hand.)

chapters.title_en: The Song He Wrote For You
chapters.goal_en: On his most public stage, catch his most private confession
chapters.scene_en: a packed arena, the encore, all lights killed but one, him and a single acoustic guitar

options.text_en: (Mouth back to him, silently: 'then finish it. for me.')
(Press a hand to your chest and nod to him, meaning it.)
(Raise your phone in the crowd, a line on the screen for him: 'i heard it. all of it.')
"You just sang it to fifty thousand people. Saying it to one should be easy."
"We can skip it. I already know. I've known since the bus."
"No skipping. I want to hear you say it. Once. Just to me."

chapters.goal_en: Between his music and his heart, help him keep the one song he won't sell
chapters.scene_en: the label's top-floor boardroom, a contract on the glass table, executives in sharp suits

options.text_en: "Don't sign it. That line is ours. I don't want it for sale, and I won't let you sell yourself either."
"It's your song. Whatever you choose, I'm walking out of here with you."
"If losing that song means keeping the real you — burn the contract."
Not tonight. Play me the rest of it instead.
(Hold out your hand, waiting for him to take it.) "Then we do it without a label. I've heard what you make alone. It's better."
"Let them drop you. The stuff that matters was never theirs anyway."
"Don't torch your whole career for me. I'm not worth your music."

chapters.goal_en: Hear him sing the last line of the song he wrote for you
chapters.scene_en: a tiny underground livehouse — no contract, no flashbulbs, a few dozen people who actually came to listen

options.text_en: "I'm yours. But that song's not finished — you're gonna write the rest of it with me."
"I've been yours since the bus. You were just too busy denying it to notice."
(Slide your hand into his and kiss him in front of everyone.)
Say it again tomorrow, sober, in daylight.

fushen.logline_en: The whole city looks up to him, and no one dares come close — until you become the only one he reaches for.
hold_en: He says nothing. The silence is not a wall this time; it is an invitation, and you can tell the difference now.
"Continue," he says. It is the closest he gets to please.
He sets his glass down without a sound and waits.
"I'm listening," he says, and he is — completely, which from him is rare.

chapters.title_en: The Distance of One Glass of Wine
chapters.goal_en: Make this man who never explains himself say more than three sentences to you
chapters.scene_en: by the floor-to-ceiling window of a penthouse, the city glittering below, wine in hand

options.text_en: "I only wanted to find the way out."
"Someone who wants nothing — does that unsettle you?"
"That glass you poured me. Already got it."
"Does that mean I can come up again?"
(Pick up the card. Say nothing. Just look at him.)
"I can take the stairs."

chapters.title_en: He Explains Himself to No One
chapters.goal_en: See what that coldness is really guarding against
chapters.scene_en: a business gala, chandeliers and champagne, everyone angling to reach him

options.text_en: "I think you're the kind who'd rather be misunderstood than bother to explain."
"I don't believe rumors. I believe what I see."
"You don't explain yourself — so how would I know?"
"Give me a ride?"
"I'll grab a cab — you go ahead."
"You're… not in a good mood today, are you."

chapters.title_en: The Young Madam of the Old House
chapters.goal_en: Find your footing in the world he never brings anyone into
chapters.scene_en: the century-old Fu family estate on the city's edge, carved verandas, rows of staff, everything heavy with old propriety

options.text_en: "If you did — I don't mind."
"You never bother to explain — but this, you let stand."
"Fu Shen. Just say it — do you want me to stay?"
"Then aren't you cold?"
(Pull the coat close, catch up, and walk at his side.)
"Fu Shen — you're actually very gentle."

chapters.goal_en: Between the family's rules and him, take the heaviest blow for him
chapters.scene_en: the grand hall of the Fu estate, the elders seated at the head, an arranged marriage laid on the table

options.text_en: "What I want, the Fu family can't afford." (Push the cheque back.)
"I'm not someone he brought in. Everyone in this house calls me Young Madam."
"The arranged match is your rule. But whom he chooses is his freedom."
Stay where you are. Just — don't go back behind the glass.
(Hug him from behind.) "I came in for you. Not for this family."
"Today you turned against your whole family for me. That's not humiliating me."
"Fu Shen. Look at me. I didn't leave. And I won't."

chapters.title_zh: 他愿意暖起来的那座房子
chapters.goal_en: Get this man who never says 'I need' to say what he truly wants
chapters.scene_en: the terrace of the Fu estate at dawn — for the first time, no staff hovering, just the two of you and a pot of coffee

options.text_en: (Put your hand in his.) "Then stay. And let this house warm up."
"You can say it. I'm here."
"Take London. It's better for the family."
Answer London first. Then ask me.

endings.title_en: The House That Was Cold for Thirty Years
A Man Who Thaws an Inch at a Time
